why: Persian distinguishes an informal second person (تو: «تلاش کن») from a formal one (شما: «تلاش کنید»).
This file records which one each section speaks, so drift fails a build instead of accumulating.
The voice was chosen by the product owner, not by this checker: sessions and the programme address
the athlete as شما. The checker's job is to keep that true, and to fail on any new section that
does not say which voice it speaks.

observed.note: Measured by tools/copy/register.mjs, not asserted. 339 strings, 7 informal, 20 formal.
observed.pattern: Sessions and the programme address the athlete as شما — decided by the product owner. Onboarding and goal declaration remain informal (تو): they are the first-run experience and read as a deliberately warmer voice. That split is now declared rather than accidental; converting those two as well is a one-line change here plus the strings the checker would then list. The coach surface is formal for a reason of its own rather than by default: it addresses a coach ABOUT a third party, and an informal voice there would read as familiarity with someone the reader may barely know.

howToResolve: All sections are decided. To change one, edit its value here and run `pnpm copy:register`;
it lists exactly which strings violate the new declaration.
